title: Scale controller token rotation caused delayed node registration and temporary reserved-pool shortfall
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers experienced transient capacity shortfalls in reserved pools during a high-traffic surge window. Symptoms looked like soft-throttles and increased 429/503 errors even though GPU headroom existed. Investigation traced the issue to the scale-controller failing to register new worker nodes because of an edge-case during service-token rotation.

Detailed timeline and reproduction:
- 2026-03-02 22:05 UTC: several customers reported elevated error rates and higher latency from Dedicated. Alerts for queue depth and token wait increased.
- 2026-03-02 22:10 UTC: on-call confirmed reserved-pool available node count reported lower than expected but infra metrics (GPU utilization, cloud VMs active) showed new VMs were spun up.
- 2026-03-02 22:25 UTC: manual inspection showed node agents were repeatedly failing TLS handshake with the scale-controller due to service-token mismatch during an automated rotation window. The controller rejected registration handshakes for a ~45s window.
- Repro: trigger a token-rotation in staging while simultaneously simulating a burst of scale-ups. Nodes started during rotation do not complete registration if they connect during a rotation commit race.

Root cause hypothesis and confirmation:
- The scale-controller performs rolling rotations of the service-issued tokens used by node agents. During a narrow race where token A is being revoked and token B is being published, the controller temporarily enforces a strict token check that rejects agent hello messages signed with token B until the controller has finished updating its in-memory signer cache. This happened when controller leader briefly GC'd signer state after an optimization change (PR #1187).
- New nodes were created by the cloud autoscaler and attempted to register within that window. Because registration failed, controller did not account for them when computing available headroom and therefore refused to authoritatively allocate burst slots for incoming tenant requests. The customers experienced capacity shortfall despite new VMs being present.

Scope and customers affected:
- A small subset of Dedicated tenants with burst-heavy traffic arriving during controller token rotations. We validated reports from 4 customers (IDs redacted), two of which are enterprise customers on Reserved pools.

Immediate mitigations performed (hotfix):
- Rolled back PR #1187 to restore the tolerant signer-cache behavior (hotfix deployed 2026-03-02 23:15 UTC).
- Issued a manual re-issue of service tokens and performed a controlled leader restart to force re-registration of node agents (recovery completed 2026-03-02 23:42 UTC).
- Opened temporary fallback: for the next 24 hours we allowed the allocator to count cloud VM heartbeats (last-seen telemetry) as provisional capacity when registration fails for <2m to reduce customer-visible throttles.

Fix implemented:
- Engineering patch adds a dual-acceptance window during token rotation: controller will accept both old and new signer tokens for 90s while ensuring signer state flush is fully persisted. This eliminates the race. Patch lives in branch fix/token-rotation-accept-window, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scale-controller/pull/1294.
- Added unit tests for token rotation and an e2e test that exercises node registration while rotation is in-flight.
- Added metrics and an alert for "node-registration-failures-during-rotation" with slowness classification so SRE can detect early.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Canary rollout (5% leaders) starting 2026-03-15 to validate in low-risk clusters.
- Gradual ramp to 100% over 6 hours if no regression.
- Post-deploy synthetic workload to simulate registration bursts and assert no registration failures in the 90s window.

Customer comms and followups:
- Customer-facing incident summary drafted and sent to affected accounts on 2026-03-04. Engineering provided steps taken and the planned release date for the permanent fix.
- Account teams offered a one-time credit and remediation meeting to discuss reliability guarantees.

Action items (postmortem style):
- (A1) Add a pre-rotation canary that applies token change to a single non-leader controller to validate signer cache persistence before cluster-wide rotation. Owner: SRE. Due: 2026-03-21.
- (A2) Revisit the allocator fallback policy: make provisional capacity behavior opt-in per-tenant and surface explicit telemetry. Owner: Allocator team. Due: 2026-04-04.
- (A3) Harden signers' in-memory cache persistence so GC cannot evict during active rotations. Owner: Scale-controller. Due: 2026-03-18.

Links to artifacts:
- Slack thread: #ops-incidents thread ID: C12345.
- Hotfix PR (rollback): https://github.com/redwood-inference/scale-controller/pull/1189 (rolled back).
- Permanent fix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scale-controller/pull/1294.

acceptance_criteria: 1) No node-registration TLS handshake failures during a controlled token rotation in staging for 30 consecutive runs. 2) Canary clusters show <1% variance in registration latency vs baseline. 3) New metric for registration-during-rotation fires and is routed to SRE pager.
resolution: Hotfix rollback restored capacity immediately. Permanent fix implemented and merged; canary rollout planned. Postmortem actions scheduled and customer communications issued.
